dct_description_sm: Zooplankton plays a pivotal role in the aquatic ecosystems as the link between primary producers and higher trophic levels such fishes, whales and birds. These relationships are driven by zooplankters' distribution, biomass and composition. In order to characterize the vertical and spatial distribution of zooplankton across the Canadian Beaufort Sea, samples were collected across both longitudinal and latitudinal gradient. Smaller taxa were collected with a 150 m Hydrobios MultiNet sampler that allows for vertical distribution study. Larger zooplankton was collected with a 500 m Bongo net that was towed obliquely. Combination of information obtained from these two sampling tools provides a wide spectrum of abundance, biomass and biodiversity data. Samples were collected from as shallow as 20 m to about 1000 m of depth. Such a wide coverage of environmental conditions will serve as a baseline for the proposed industrial development to happen in the Canadian Beaufort Sea.
dct_title_s: Beaufort Regional Environmental Assessment (BREA) Marine Fishes Project - Zooplankton data collected from the Canadian Beaufort Sea August to September 2013
